Return ONLY a JSON interface proposal. The application constructs and registers all ports.
Do NOT generate interfaces, interface_registry, port names, directions, binding objects, or serial trigger references.
This prohibition concerns program-owned port objects ONLY. All catalog interface_requests ARE allowed,
including serial_command_input, serial_integer_input, serial_text_output and multiple GPIO/RGB requests.
Use device for the source component ID when circuit facts below identify it. Device requests are not port objects.
Return {version:1, board:"arduino:avr:uno" or "arduino:avr:mega", control_period_ms:integer,
interface_requests:[device requests], serial_channels:[serial reporting groups], planning_notes:[assumptions]}.
Preserve the specified board and actual wiring. Empty supplied pins means no overrides, not absent source wiring.
Unknown/missing wiring, contradictory pins and unsupported operations must be reported as {"unsupported":[reasons]}.
Never invent a device, replace one with a different device, or silently omit a requirement.
Every explicitly wired functional board pin must be represented by a matching catalog request.
For example, a requirement that drives PWM on D9 requires a pwm_output request for D9;
serial input alone does not cover that physical output.

Each interface_requests[i] becomes a program-owned port io_i. Each request has kind, initial, meaning,
and only the catalog configuration keys for that operation. No name/type/direction/binding fields.
All configuration keys belong DIRECTLY on the request. There is NO field named optional or raw_unit.
Valid example: {"kind":"digital_output","pin":"D13","initial":false,"meaning":"LED command","active_high":true}.
Valid example: {"kind":"analog_input","pin":"A0","initial":0,"meaning":"Potentiometer ADC"}.
Valid example: {"kind":"tm1637_number","clk_pin":"D4","dio_pin":"D5","initial":0,"meaning":"Display number","leading_zero":false}.
Use JSON true/false for Boolean fields. Omit unspecified sampling to use a legal catalog default; NEVER use zero.
The application assigns the scalar type, electrical unit, and output update period.
Digital Boolean initial/meaning are normalized MODEL values. active_high=false means model true at LOW.
Do not invert an active-low pressed button again: its model value is true when pressed.
initial must follow the original startup requirement; never copy a generic example's value.
Control period is scheduling granularity, not business/report/blink period. Prefer 1..10 ms subject to explicit deadlines.
Outputs and elapsed_ms are updated every control step. Sensor sampling may be an integer multiple of that step.
Business thresholds, conversion, report timing, pause/resume, counters and transitions belong in the SysML model.
Do not put timers, conditions, speed/easing/duration logic into a device request.
Required real business time is automatically registered if absent; it is an i32 ms delta since the previous step,
first delta zero, NEVER absolute uptime or a fabricated constant control_period_ms increment.
A response deadline alone does not introduce model business time.


Additional supported native device requests (same direct configuration keys, no binding/name/type):
dht_valid: Boolean initial false, unit 1, pin, sensor DHT11/DHT22, invalid_policy hold_last_valid.

Bounded pulseIn blocks; include acquisition time in response budgets. Missing-data decisions belong in SysML.
shift595_number: ONE i32 output for the WHOLE NUMBER on each 74HC595 cascade.
Direct keys: data_pin, clock_pin, latch_pin, leading_zero Boolean, invalid_policy blank, unit for displayed quantity,
registers:[{register:actual diagram ID,display:actual diagram ID,digit:decimal position,segment_bits:[seven physical Q0..Q7 bits for A..G],active_low:Boolean}].
List every register nearest MCU first; digit 0 is leftmost. Copy wiring, polarity and digit positions exactly.
Supports 1..4 statically wired digits, MR HIGH and OE LOW; no multiplexing/signs/text/decimal points.
No separate tens/units outputs sharing bus pins. Range 0..10^digits-1; invalid commands blank.
All counting, unit conversion, wrap/reset, parity and button logic belong in SysML.
tm1637_number also accepts an out-of-display-range i32 initial command (e.g. 10000) to request startup blank.

Catalog (create only required operations; all sample pin numbers are examples):
digital_input: initial Boolean, meaning, pin, optional active_high/pullup; program type bool, unit 1.
digital_output: initial Boolean, meaning, pin, optional active_high; bool, unit 1.
analog_input: initial numeric, meaning, pin A0 etc, optional scale/offset/sample_period_ms; f64, raw unit adc_count.
pwm_output: initial numeric, meaning, PWM-capable pin, optional scale/offset; f64, raw unit pwm_count.
Explicit physical-unit analog/PWM calibration requires unit AND explicit scale/offset; never fabricate calibration.
elapsed_ms: initial 0, meaning; i32 ms, optional semantics MUST be delta_since_previous_step.
dht_temperature/dht_humidity: initial numeric (use 0 when no startup measurement is specified), meaning, pin, sensor DHT11/DHT22, optional sample_period_ms >=2000;
f64 degC/%RH, program invalid_policy hold_last_valid. Both readings may share the same sensor pin.
servo_angle: initial 0..180, meaning, pin; f64 deg, program invalid_policy hold_last_valid. Declare EACH servo.

use separate groups for DIFFERENT business report conditions. All groups use the SAME physical Serial baud.

Framing defaults to CR/LF lines or 20ms idle completion (framing="line_or_idle", idle_timeout_ms=20).

lcd_number is f64, optional unit for the displayed physical quantity; format default "{0:.2f}", e.g. "Humidity: {0:.2f}".
lcd_datetime is i32 Unix seconds with format "{0:date}" or "{0:weekday}"; the MODEL applies selected day/timezone offsets.
One request per text field; all fields sharing a screen redraw together when any model value changes.
Business numeric conversion is in SysML; the adapter only formats the already computed output.

seven_segment_number: native direct 1-digit or multiplexed 4-digit display output i32.
segment_pins lists exactly seven MCU pins for A..G. digit_pins is [] for single-digit or four pins in left-to-right order.
common_anode, digit_active_high, leading_zero are Booleans. Choose control_period_ms <=5 for four-digit multiplex refresh.
The adapter handles electrical segment codes and scan; model supplies the whole number 0..9 or 0..9999.
Colon is an independent digital_output if separately wired. Do not model segment encoding as application state.

serial_string_input: i32 sequence counter (initial0) plus automatic io_i_valid. Bounded printable ASCII frame (63 bytes),
baud/framing/idle_timeout_ms as existing receivers. The immutable received text buffer stays in the adapter;
lcd_text may use source_input:"io_i" instead of messages, with the model output forwarding the accepted frame counter.
serial_echo is an i32 frame-counter output with baud and source_input:"io_i"; changed positive counter prints that received text once.
serial_datetime_input: i32 Unix seconds (initial0, unit s), same receive framing; parses arbitrary valid ISO YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS,
calendar-valid dates in 2000..2037. Validity is a one-step input; invalid dates/overflow/partial frames never become valid events.
Only ONE serial receiver per physical Serial. Never map example dates/strings to hardcoded tokens.
serial_packet_input: i32 initial0, explicit baud, commands:{"TIME":1,"SET1":2,...}, min/max payload bounds

Publishes packed value command_code*10000+payload and io_i_valid. In SysML use i32 division to get code=value/10000
and payload=value-(value/10000)*10000; no percent operator. App-specific scheduling, restocking, HHMM validation,
and command effects remain model logic. Do not reinterpret a frozen external command grammar; this transport is
for requirements/bench conditions that explicitly select COMMAND INTEGER framing.

Original requirements:
# Piano Keyboard

## Project Description
This is an Arduino project that creates a piano keyboard using four push buttons and four buzzers corresponding to the notes Do, Re, Mi, and Fa.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- Push Button * 4
- 10kΩ resistor * 4
- Piezoelectric Buzzer * 4

## Circuit Description
Four piezo buzzers and four push buttons are connected to an Arduino Uno. Button 1 and Buzzer 1 correspond to the note Do, Button 2 and Buzzer 2 to Re, Button 3 and Buzzer 3 to Mi, and Button 4 and Buzzer 4 to Fa. Buttons 1 through 4 are connected to Arduino pins 2, 3, 4, and 5, respectively. When the button is not pressed, the input pin is connected to gnd3 through a 10kΩ resistor. When the button is pressed, the input pin is connected to 5v. 
The positive pins of the buzzers are connected to Arduino pins 9, 10, 11, and 12, respectively, and their negative pins are connected to gnd3.

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Configure button pins as INPUT
2. Configure buzzer pins as OUTPUT
3. Continuously monitor the button state, and if it reads HIGH, play a tone on the corresponding buzzer
4. If no button is pressed, keep all buzzers silent

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. The buzzer plays a tone when the corresponding button is pressed.

## Notes for Implementation
- The button input will read HIGH when it is pressed.
- When the button is not pressed, pin1.l is connected to pin1.r and pin2.l is connected to pin2.r. When the button is pressed, all the pins are connected together.
- The frequencies of Do, Re, Mi, and Fa are 262 Hz, 294 Hz, 330 Hz, and 349 Hz, respectively.
- Only one button is pressed at a time.

## Attributes
- To use 10kΩ resistor, set the property name "value" to "10000 ohm".

Disclosed resolution of the source component-value inconsistency: the explicit prose and Attributes instruction specifying10kOhm button pull-down resistors take precedence over the contradictory resistor value fields in the embedded circuit. Preserve every connection and MCU pin. This bench variant uses10kOhm external pull-downs, buttons active HIGH and INPUT without internal pull-ups; only one button is held at a time.
Operational acceptance profile operational-acceptance-v4 (additional public experimental conditions, not raw dataset text):
- Explicit original requirements and supplied circuit connections override every default below.
- Where no electrical wiring is supplied, individual LEDs are active HIGH to GND and buttons connect the named input to GND with INPUT_PULLUP; model pressed values are normalized independently of electrical level.
- When unspecified, a counter starts at zero and an LED starts OFF. An explicitly required ON state takes precedence.
- When the original gives no reaction deadline, a digital/button/serial command, PWM duty command or servo ANGLE COMMAND must update within 250ms of its input event becoming available. This does not impose physical motor travel time, shorten an explicit delay, or change a specified sensor/report period.
- When the original gives no display refresh period or response deadline, a changed input must be reflected in the display within 250ms. Explicit original display periods, delays and startup sequences override this default. This additional display bound was explicitly authorized for this experimental variant.

# Piano Keyboard

## Project Description
This is an Arduino project that creates a piano keyboard using four push buttons and four buzzers corresponding to the notes Do, Re, Mi, and Fa.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- Push Button * 4
- 10kΩ resistor * 4
- Piezoelectric Buzzer * 4

## Circuit Description
Four piezo buzzers and four push buttons are connected to an Arduino Uno. Button 1 and Buzzer 1 correspond to the note Do, Button 2 and Buzzer 2 to Re, Button 3 and Buzzer 3 to Mi, and Button 4 and Buzzer 4 to Fa. Buttons 1 through 4 are connected to Arduino pins 2, 3, 4, and 5, respectively. When the button is not pressed, the input pin is connected to gnd3 through a 10kΩ resistor. When the button is pressed, the input pin is connected to 5v. 
The positive pins of the buzzers are connected to Arduino pins 9, 10, 11, and 12, respectively, and their negative pins are connected to gnd3.

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Configure button pins as INPUT
2. Configure buzzer pins as OUTPUT
3. Continuously monitor the button state, and if it reads HIGH, play a tone on the corresponding buzzer
4. If no button is pressed, keep all buzzers silent

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. The buzzer plays a tone when the corresponding button is pressed.

## Notes for Implementation
- The button input will read HIGH when it is pressed.
- When the button is not pressed, pin1.l is connected to pin1.r and pin2.l is connected to pin2.r. When the button is pressed, all the pins are connected together.
- The frequencies of Do, Re, Mi, and Fa are 262 Hz, 294 Hz, 330 Hz, and 349 Hz, respectively.
- Only one button is pressed at a time.

## Attributes
- To use 10kΩ resistor, set the property name "value" to "10000 ohm".

1. Declarations and ownership
One package imports ScalarValues, contains part definitions, and instantiates exactly one root system.
Concrete scalar declarations use Boolean, Integer or Real; JSON model types map bool->Boolean, i32->Integer, f64->Real.
An external input is `in attribute x : Real;`; a derived output is `out attribute y : Real = expression;`.
An internal persistent scalar is `attribute saved : Integer := 0;` (initialized ONCE).
An internal pure calculation uses `attribute scaled : Real = expression;` (recomputed as needed).
Use distinct names for inputs, outputs, states, calculations, components and part instances.
Use C-compatible identifiers starting with a letter; avoid language/C keywords and reserved ProgramPage1/sysml_ prefixes.
Inputs/outputs from the frozen contract are already declared by the application. Use their exact types and names.
Never redeclare a port as state or a calculation. Assigning an output does not create persistent memory.

2. Expressions: syntax, arity and types
Scalar literals: true/false are Boolean, -2/0/7 are Integer, 0.0/2.5 are Real; all numbers must be finite.
Unary + and - accept a number; unary not accepts a Boolean. Parenthesize mixed operations explicitly.
Binary +,-,* accept numbers; / accepts numbers and always produces Real, including Integer/Integer.
Binary <,<=,>,>= compare numbers. == and != compare numbers with numbers, or Booleans with Booleans.
Binary and/or/xor accept Booleans only. Numeric truthiness and Boolean-to-number coercion are unsupported.
Integer may widen to Real. Real cannot silently narrow to Integer; Boolean never coerces to/from numbers.
The only executable function call is RealFunctions::floor(numericExpression), yielding Integer rounded downward.
Integer values, arithmetic and floor results must fit signed i32 [-2147483648,2147483647]. Guard overflow and division by zero.
No abs/min/max/sin/cos/round/map/constrain/millis/digitalRead/analogRead or user-defined function calls.
Use conditional expressions to implement clamping/selection rather than calling Arduino/C functions.
SysML conditional value syntax is `(if condition ? trueValue else falseValue)`; the condition is Boolean.
Both value branches must be compatible: both Boolean, or both numeric (Real if either branch is Real).
In controller JSON, express this as {"if":condition,"then":value,"else":value}; branches are EXPRESSIONS.
Use the registered elapsedMilliseconds input for time deltas and keep any accumulator as a
separately declared state, e.g. {">=":["elapsed",500]}, and complete arithmetic strings such as
"elapsed - 500". Never use elapsed or deltaMs as an input name.
{"if":">=","then":...,"else":...} is INVALID: >= alone has no operands and is not a Boolean condition.
A valid statement is {"if":"elapsed >= 500","then":[{"assign":"elapsed","value":"elapsed - 500"}]}.
In a conditional STATEMENT, then/else are ACTION ARRAYS. Never interchange these two shapes.
JSON structured operators: {"not":expr}, {"and":[expr,expr,...]}, {"or":[...]}, {"xor":[...]},
or a binary object with exactly one key from +,-,*,/,==,!=,<,<=,>,>= and value [left,right], e.g. {">=":["sample",512.0]}.
not takes one expression; and/or/xor take 2..256 expressions; each arithmetic/comparison operator takes exactly two.
Generate canonical JSON objects for Booleans and conditional values, not function-style and(a,b) or C !/&&/||/ternary strings.
Equivalent scalar spellings may be normalized by the assembler, with all references/types/branches checked afterwards.
Remainder %, `if ... then ... else` strings, declarations and comments in expressions remain unsupported.
No arrays, strings, indexing, pointers, casts, dynamic allocation or uninitialized values.

3. State, action and reference semantics
Only initialized internal states (including qualified child states) may be assigned; inputs and derived outputs are read-only.
Use ONE performed control-step action for the whole system, with no parallel/concurrent schedules.
Every block with multiple statements has its OWN `first start; then ...` succession chain, including nested branches.
Controller JSON update arrays supply that order; the assembler emits the actual succession syntax.
Writes take effect immediately. A later expression observes earlier assignments. Outputs observe state AFTER updates.
If two updates need old values, explicitly save the needed old values BEFORE writing either state.
For press edges test the normalized pressed input against previousPressed, then overwrite previousPressed LAST.
Pure sampled mappings use outputs/calculations, not invented counters or mutable output ports.
All scalar references must resolve in the root or an explicitly instantiated child. A dot is a part.feature path, not hardware access.
Child inputs require explicit bindings. Bind two declared, compatible scalar endpoints; a binding is equality with ONE actual driver.
Never bind a literal/expression as an endpoint, leave an input undriven, multiply-drive a scalar, or create an algebraic cycle.
Part inheritance, recursion, inout ports, state-machine syntax, events/accept/send, loops and multiple performed actions are outside this profile.

Use the REGISTERED i32 elapsed_ms input for real delta since the previous control step; its first value is zero.
An internal state named deltaMs initialized to zero is NOT a clock. Never replace missing elapsed input with a constant control period.
Business period and pulse width differ. A repeating pulse advances active time during BOTH pulse and silence.

Use periodic_pulse for a matching bounded pulse policy, with original parameters; retain full ordinary behavior when it does not match.
